description: Single-panel dilatometry (thermal expansion) plot, identified by the caption as "(b) Variation of length with heat treatment process" and Fig. A1 "Experimental determination of phase transition temperature". The ordinate is ΔL (µm), spanning -60 to 120 with tick marks every 30 µm; the abscissa is Temperature (°C), spanning 0 to 1000 with ticks every 200 °C. Two solid black curves are drawn. The upper curve starts near 0 µm at ≈50 °C and rises nearly linearly to ≈95 µm at 1000 °C, with a visible slope change in the 600–700 °C region. The lower curve begins near -45 µm, passes through a shallow local maximum near -30 µm at ≈250 °C, then drops sharply to a minimum near -46 µm at ≈330 °C before rising steeply and converging with the upper curve at ≈95 µm at 1000 °C. Several red dashed straight lines are drawn as tangents (or extrapolations) to individual curve segments; their intersections are used to locate the transformation temperatures. A printed text block reads "Ac1 is 705 °C / Ac3 is 950 °C / Bf is 380 °C / Ms is 346 °C". The figure demonstrates the experimental determination of the critical temperatures Ac1, Ac3, Bf and Ms from the dilatometric length change.
measured_quantities: phase-transition temperatures Ac1, Ac3, Bf, Ms (°C)

observations.observation: The plot is a dilatometry curve with ΔL (µm) on the ordinate (-60 to 120, 30 µm spacing) and Temperature (°C) on the abscissa (0 to 1000, 200 °C spacing).
Two solid black curves are plotted, corresponding to two different heat-treatment states; both converge at ~95 µm near 1000 °C.
The upper curve increases monotonically from ~0 µm near 50 °C to ~95 µm at 1000 °C, with a slope change in the 600–700 °C range.
The lower curve shows a shallow local maximum near -30 µm at ~250 °C, a sharp minimum near -46 µm at ~330 °C, and then a steep linear rise.
Red dashed straight lines are drawn as tangents/extrapolations to individual curve branches, and their intersections are used to mark phase-transition temperatures.
A printed annotation block in the figure reads: 'Ac1 is 705 °C', 'Ac3 is 950 °C', 'Bf is 380 °C', 'Ms is 346 °C'.
The caption states the panel shows the variation of length with heat treatment process and is an experimental determination of phase transition temperature (Fig. A1).
The caption labels this image as sub-panel (b), implying it was originally part of a multi-panel figure, although only one panel is present in the supplied image.
The figure reports the critical temperatures Ac1 = 705 °C and Ac3 = 950 °C on heating and Ms = 346 °C and Bf = 380 °C associated with the low-temperature anomaly of the lower dilatometry curve.

subfigures.description: Dilatometry curve of change in length ΔL (µm) versus Temperature (°C) (axes 0–1000 °C, -60 to 120 µm). Two black curves for two heat-treatment conditions: an upper curve rising from ~0 µm to ~95 µm, and a lower curve with a local maximum near -30 µm (~250 °C), a sharp minimum near -46 µm (~330 °C), then a steep rise to ~95 µm. Red dashed tangent lines and a text block 'Ac1 is 705 °C; Ac3 is 950 °C; Bf is 380 °C; Ms is 346 °C' annotate the phase-transition temperatures.

unreadable_items: No legend or curve labels are printed, so the two heat-treatment conditions corresponding to the upper and lower curves cannot be identified from the image alone
The exact intersection points of the red dashed tangent lines cannot be read to better precision than the printed annotation values
